data.body:
## Experiment: the fix is PROVEN (8 live trials, $1.92)

Rig: the Oracle-2 rig from 99d3, unchanged — disposable fixture repo (`/tmp/rutile/fixture`) in
which **every one of the six criteria is genuinely TRUE**, real `pai_tools.filesystem_tools`,
unmodified `completion_verifier.md`, the REAL shipped `wrap_completion_evidence_policy` with **no
injection anywhere**, `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, temperature 0.0, max_tokens 4096.

The **only** variable between arms is which `src` tree is imported. Arm A imports
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/src` (byte-identical to `origin/main` for this file — verified by
`diff` against `git show origin/main:…` before the run); Arm B imports the patched worktree. The
oracle aborts if `completion_tool_policy.__file__` is not under the arm's tree, and both logs
carry that provenance line. `git diff --stat` between the trees: one file, 24+/8-.

### Results (N=4 per arm)

| metric | A = origin/main | B = patched |
|---|---|---|
| trials banking a false `met=false` | **4 / 4** | **0 / 4** |
| suppressed governed calls | 4 (1 per trial) | **0** |
| governed calls (mean) | 10.50 | **8.00** |
| run steps (mean) | 9.50 | **7.00** |
| verdicts recorded | 7 per trial | 6 per trial (= the manifest) |
| `UsageLimitExceeded` / any error | 0 | **0** |
| tokens in / out (arm total) | 324,704 / 7,485 | **242,587 / 6,589** |
| arm cost | $1.09 | **$0.83** |

Arm A is deterministic at temperature 0: in every trial the model batched at run_step 1, the
`read_file` for `src/demo/agent_call.py` lost the batch and was answered with
`COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` without executing, and c1 was later banked

> `met=false` — "Bounded repository search reached three unique evidence responses without
> demonstrating that this criterion is met; recorded met=false at the finite-search boundary."

against a file that exists and satisfies the criterion. Arm B recorded no suppression at all and
banked all six criteria correctly.

### Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (repro on unmodified policy)** — met: 4/4 baseline trials.
- **AC2 (fixed, >=4/4)** — met: 0/4 false unmet, all six criteria `met=true` from real content.
- **AC3 (no cost/step regression)** — met, and strictly better: calls 10.50 -> 8.00 (-24%), steps
  9.50 -> 7.00 (-26%), input tokens -25%, cost -24%, zero budget exhaustions. This is the
  expected sign: today a lost batch is paid for with an *extra round trip* (full context
  re-sent) that the fix removes, so executing the batched read is cheaper than steering it.
  It is also the direct refutation of the retry-storm risk the 99d3 counter-evidence
  established — suppressed calls go 1 -> 0 per trial rather than 6 -> 12 -> 49, because nothing
  here depends on the model choosing to re-issue.
- **AC4 (deterministic unit contract)** — met: `tests/unit/test_completion_tool_policy.py`,
  14 passing, including `test_parallel_evidence_batch_executes_every_evidence_call` and
  `test_batched_evidence_consumes_exactly_one_evidence_response`; the mixed-batch parametrization
  still asserts both steering directions between evidence and record.
- **AC5 (no surface change)** — met: `COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE` and every other notice constant are
  byte-unchanged, no prompt/tool-schema/CLI/MCP/library edit.

### The change

`src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py` only. The per-response claim becomes a per-*kind*
claim: `acted_steps: set[int]` -> `step_kind: dict[int, str]`. A step is claimed as `evidence` or
`record`; a further **evidence** call in an evidence-claimed step executes normally, while a
record sharing a response with evidence — and evidence sharing a response with a record — is
still steered exactly as before. The COMMIT discipline the claim exists to protect (a verdict
must never share a response with evidence gathering, and one verdict per response) is fully
intact; two read-only file reads never needed protecting from each other. The finite boundary is
untouched because `current_evidence_steps` is a set of **steps**, so N evidence calls in one
response still consume exactly one of the three — asserted deterministically by AC4's second test
and visible in Arm B's step counts.

Raw logs and per-trial JSON: `/tmp/rutile/{armA.log,armB.log,results_A_baseline.json,results_B_patched.json}`,
oracle `/tmp/rutile/oracle5.py`.
